Objective: Determine whether any dataset behind the field-diagnostic copilot is ready to train or fine-tune on, and what must be true — on coverage, quality, labels, access, and provenance — before we commit modeling spend to a company-wide build.

Body: I cannot fully close this yet — the task is undefined. "Is the data good enough" only has an answer once we know which equipment lines the model must diagnose, what accuracy threshold counts as safe, and the target architecture consuming the data. Domain Owner and architecture decisions must land first. What follows is what I can say now.

**Dataset 1 — Pilot repair logs (FSM export, pilot period).** Coverage against the full equipment catalog is unknown [ASSUMPTION: pilot covered a subset of lines/technicians — validate against FSM asset registry]. Quality: "known issues" cited but no measured error/null rate against a named denominator exists — that's a placeholder, not a finding. Labels: this is where the programme dies. Disagreements were "rarely logged" — informal calls and silent overrides. Ground truth for "was the copilot wrong" barely exists for this period. **Decision: withheld.**

**Dataset 2 — Historical repair records (pre-pilot).** These encode the old process, including senior-tech workarounds and possible inconsistent treatment by region, equipment age, or tenure. Whether that's disparate treatment is not mine to call — goes to the Governance Advisor before touching a baseline model. **Decision: conditional, pending governance review.**

**Dataset 3 — Escalation/override records — HARD GATE.** No rollout date may be set until this closes; it is not parallel-track work. Building it requires forward-logging every disagreement now, plus retrospective relabeling of the pilot period by senior technicians. Estimate: 4–6 technicians, 6–8 weeks, [ASSUMPTION: $40–70K loaded cost, derived from ~pilot ticket volume × assumed hours-per-relabel × loaded technician rate — validate both inputs against actuals]. Their field workload must be backfilled — proposed owner: Field Ops Manager schedules coverage before relabeling starts. Labeler disagreements go to a named senior reviewer (proposed: Process Excellence lead) for adjudication, logged with rationale. Critically: a labeler's call being later overridden by the rollout decision must not affect their standing — this needs an explicit statement from leadership, not an assumption. Nobody currently owns this dataset. **Decision: withheld until built.**

**Dataset 4 — FSM integration feed.** Access readiness depends on the integration blueprint and architecture, not yet decided. Provenance: presumably company-owned; confirm whether FSM is vendor-hosted, whether the DPA covers training use, and whether technician identifiers are personal data requiring Privacy sign-off.

**Bias/AI Act:** Repair guidance is safety-adjacent, which means checking against the AI Act's high-risk framework, but the cited source is a general overview — it does not establish that this specific system falls under an Annex III category or safety-component provision. That mapping is Legal's determination, not mine, and must happen before architecture is locked.

Citations: https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/high-level-summary/

Risks: Training on pilot logs as-is means the model learns from a period where disagreements went unlogged — it reproduces the silent-override blind spot at scale, and nobody will know it's wrong until a technician follows bad guidance. Historical records likely represent less-experienced technicians and less-common equipment lines worst, since that's where workarounds concentrate — those populations get the poorest performance and least visibility. If AI Act classification stays unresolved past architecture selection, we may have to re-architect for compliance after spend. If Dataset 3's gate is treated as one workstream among many rather than a blocker, leadership may set a rollout date the data cannot support.

Next Steps: (1) Domain Owner specifies the diagnostic task and accuracy threshold — required before final readiness. (2) Field Ops Manager arranges technician backfill; Process Excellence lead owns disagreement adjudication and golden dataset build, 6–8 weeks — no rollout date set until this closes. (3) Governance Advisor reviews historical records for differential treatment before baseline modeling. (4) Legal rules on AI Act classification against specific provisions before architecture is locked. (5) IT/Data Governance confirms FSM data-processing terms and grants scoped access once (1)–(4) close.
